summary: A Class C felony failure to stop at the direction of a peace officer was charged at Fairbanks on Oct. 14 and arraigned the same afternoon, alongside a Class A misdemeanour drink-driving count. Eight Fairbanks cases were filed on Wednesday, the busiest filing day in the report's window: a city prosecution for unlawful discharge of a firearm, a domestic violence assault with a warrant requested, a theft case on a $5,000 warrant, three further misdemeanours, and one number the public database refuses. A Class B felony domestic violence assault indicted on Oct. 8 was arraigned in Superior Court on Oct. 14. A change of plea was held in a North Pole domestic violence case and the hearing result is recorded as Case Disposed while the case status still reads Reopened and no disposition is printed against any count. A judgment was entered in a separate North Pole domestic violence case indicted in April, which this record had not previously carried. A Class C felony assault charge was dismissed by the prosecution on Oct. 13 and that case is closed. Two files that had carried no charging document are now charged. Troopers are investigating a death at a North Pole residence, with no cause and no manner of death stated and no crime alleged. A hit and run reported on Oct. 12 was posted by the troopers on Oct. 14 with no suspect identified. The weekly criminal charges report, run-stamped 9:00 p.m. Oct. 14, lists 47 Fairbanks cases, 3 at Nenana, 2 at Delta Junction and none at Healy for a nineteenth consecutive week; nothing arrived late onto a day already read, and eight numbers the court opened on Oct. 8 are absent from it for a sixth run. The criminal dispositions report has not refreshed in three days. Thirteen case numbers the court prints are denied by the public database, one of them new. Five case files state six charges and the database serves five, so charge counts on two of them are published as five of six with the sixth recorded as unknown. The city police bulletin added rows to six dated days, including two that had shown none. The trooper page for Oct. 15 was not published at the time of reading and no figure is carried for it. The U.S. Attorney index could not be fetched by the direct route its reading requires and was read by another non-browser route for a second morning, establishing the membership of the index and nothing finer.

entries.title: City police bulletin adds rows to six dated days, including two days it had shown as empty
body: The Fairbanks Police Department daily bulletin was read by date for Oct. 9 to Oct. 15, with the dated header and the result count confirmed on every page. Six of the seven dated pages returned more rows than the previous reading. Oct. 13 returned two rows where it had returned none on a complete calendar day; Oct. 12 returned one where it had returned none on three separate readings; Oct. 14 returned one; Oct. 11 went from two to four, Oct. 10 from three to five and Oct. 9 from six to nine. The page for Oct. 15 returned 0 Found with the header confirmed at 03:21, on a day three hours old, which is the count at the moment of reading and nothing more.

Four case numbers on those pages are new to this record. Case 26003136, Oct. 12 at 15:02, an incident classified Burglary - Non Forced at the 100 block of College Road; it is an incident report, names nobody and carries no charge. Case 26003140, Oct. 13 between 02:13 and 02:14, an incident classified Assault Simple/Other at the 1300 block of Fifth Avenue; it also names nobody. Case 26003151, Oct. 13 at 18:10, an arrest at the 500 block of First Avenue on a charge the police record as unlawful discharge of a firearm, a misdemeanour. Case 26003163, Oct. 14 at 18:14, an arrest at the 500 block of Cushman Street on a charge the police record as assault in the fourth degree, recklessly injure, a misdemeanour.

One of the four has a court file: the Oct. 13 firearm arrest is 4FA-26-02082CR, set out below. The Oct. 14 assault arrest had no court file at the time of reading, which is a statement about that reading and not about whether a file exists. Charge classes are taken from the court file and none is stated here for either police label. The bulletin covers the city of Fairbanks only, and death investigations have never appeared on it.

entries.title: Troopers investigating a death at a North Pole residence
body: The Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch, incident AK26102575, records that on Oct. 14, 2026 at approximately 17:30 troopers responded to a residence in North Pole for a report of a deceased individual, that the deceased was identified as Elijah Vandpietersom, age 28, that next of kin have been notified and that the investigation remains ongoing. The entry was posted at 11:02 p.m. on Oct. 14 and is typed Death Investigation. The name and age are as the trooper release states them.

The release states no cause and no manner of death, records no referral to the State Medical Examiner's Office, and alleges no crime. No finding has been announced by that office. A search of the public court records under that name returned no record of any kind. Nothing beyond the facts in the release is stated here.

North Pole has no municipal incident feed and the Fairbanks city bulletin carries nothing outside city limits and no death investigations at all, so a death at North Pole reaches the record through the trooper dispatch or not at all.

entries.title: Class C felony failure to stop charged at Fairbanks and arraigned the same day
body: A Fairbanks criminal case, 4FA-26-02088CR, was filed on Oct. 14 against Jeremy Frank Edwards. Count 1 is failing to stop at the direction of a peace officer by reckless driving, AS 28.35.182(a)(1), a Class C felony. Count 2 is driving under the influence with a blood alcohol content of .08 per cent or more, AS 28.35.030(a)(2), a Class A misdemeanour; the weekly charges report prints a reading of .188 against it. Both counts are offence-dated Oct. 14, 2026 at Fairbanks and neither is recorded as domestic violence related. The indicted-charge and amended-charge fields are empty on both counts, so the case is on a complaint. The case judge is Schwalm.

An arraignment was held on Oct. 14 at 1:30 p.m. in Courtroom 102, with a pre-trial risk assessment report, counsel appointed from the bench, the Public Defender Agency entered and a temporary order with release conditions. Preliminary hearings are calendared for Oct. 22 and Nov. 3, both at 3:15 p.m. in Courtroom 102. The docket carries six rows, all dated Oct. 14. He is charged, not convicted.

entries.title: Judgment entered in a North Pole domestic violence assault case indicted in April
body: A Fairbanks criminal case, 4FA-26-00703CR, against Kyle Douglas Folger, was filed on Apr. 21, 2026 and carries three counts, all offence-dated Apr. 20, 2026 with an offence location of North Pole and all recorded as domestic violence related. Count 1 is assault in the third degree, cause injury with a weapon, AS 11.41.220(a)(1)(B), a Class C felony, recorded as an indicted count with a stage date of Apr. 30, 2026. Count 2 is assault in the fourth degree, recklessly injure, a Class A misdemeanour. Count 3 is assault when a child is present, AS 11.41.240(a), a Class A misdemeanour, added by an information filed Oct. 5, 2026. The case judge is Temple.

The event list records a change of plea on Oct. 12 at 8:30 a.m. in Courtroom 201, Hearing Held, and the docket carries a criminal judgment or disposition order entered the same day. The omnibus hearing of Dec. 10 and the trial week of Jan. 4, 2027 are both now recorded Hearing Vacated. No disposition code is printed against any of the three counts and the case status reads Reopened.

The Fairbanks Daily News-Miner's public safety column of Oct. 14 reports that a man of that name and age 45 pleaded guilty to reduced charges of fourth-degree assault and assault in the presence of a child from an April case, and that with the plea change he faces two years of probation and must complete a parenting class by June 2027. The age is as the newspaper states it. The court file carries the judgment row and no disposition code; both records are stated and neither is asserted over the other. Nothing describing the conduct is reproduced and nobody recorded as a victim is identified.

entries.title: Weekly charges report: 47 Fairbanks cases, 3 at Nenana, 2 at Delta Junction, none at Healy for a nineteenth week
body: The Alaska Court System's weekly criminal charges report carries the footer stamp Report Run Date 10/14/2026 9:00 pm and the window 10/8/2026 to 10/14/2026, across 64 pages. Read in full for the four Interior court prefixes, it lists 47 cases at Fairbanks, 3 at Nenana, 2 at Delta Junction and no Healy section at all, which is a nineteenth consecutive week; the word Healy does not appear anywhere in the report, for a third consecutive week. The four courts were located by their headings and their End of lines rather than by page number, and the Fairbanks block has moved from pages 26 to 31 in the previous run to pages 25 to 30 in this one.

The Fairbanks cases fall as seven on Oct. 8, eight on Oct. 9, eight on Oct. 10, five on Oct. 11, six on Oct. 12, five on Oct. 13 and eight on Oct. 14. Every day held over from the previous run carries the same number of cases it carried then, so nothing arrived late onto a day already read. Oct. 7, which held six cases, has rolled off the seven-day window.

The offence-location column, scanned separately from the case prefixes, records 84 charge lines at Fairbanks, 5 at Delta Junction, 4 at North Pole, 1 at Nenana and 1 at Ester, and none at Fort Wainwright, Eielson, Salcha, Minto, Anderson, Clear, Healy, Two Rivers, Moose Creek or Fox. Five charge lines are recorded at Tok and four at Tanana, both outside the coverage area; the four Tanana lines sit on a case filed at the Nenana court, which is inside it.

The Fairbanks list runs contiguously from 4FA-26-02035CR to 4FA-26-02041CR and then jumps to 4FA-26-02050CR, with the numbers 02042 to 02049 absent for a sixth consecutive run. Those eight numbers resolve in the public database with a status of Open and carry no defendant, no charge, no file date and no docket row. All six runs were stamped after they were opened and this window contains Oct. 8. The report's window closes at 9 p.m. and is therefore short of its own last filing day.

entries.title: The criminal dispositions report has not refreshed in three days
body: The Alaska Court System's criminal dispositions report carries the footer stamp Data updated 10/12/2026 at 4:00 am and the header Case Closed Between 9/1/2026 to 10/12/2026, both unchanged for a third consecutive reading, on 237 pages. Walked in full for the four Interior court prefixes it carries 182 distinct Fairbanks case numbers, 11 at Nenana, 6 at Delta Junction and none at Healy, every figure identical to the previous two readings.

Freshness is read from the footer stamp and not from the page count. Nothing is inferred from an unmoved file about what the court has closed since the stamp. 4FA-26-01852CR, open since Sept. 19 with no charging document and nothing on its docket since Sept. 22, is absent from the file for a twenty-sixth day.

entries.title: Troopers post a hit-and-run from Oct. 12 two days after it was reported
body: The Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch, incident AK26101647, records that on Oct. 12, 2026 at approximately 09:08 troopers at Fairbanks received a report of a hit and run at the Sourdough gas station at the intersection of Farmers Loop and the Steese Highway. The caller reported that her vehicle was struck by a white pickup with an unidentified male driver who left the scene immediately, that camera quality was insufficient to identify the licence plate, and that the investigation is pending further leads. Nobody is named and no arrest is recorded.

The entry was posted at 9:31 a.m. on Oct. 14, two days after the incident, and onto the Oct. 14 page rather than the Oct. 12 one. It appears on no earlier dated page and in no city bulletin row. Dispatch dates are posting dates and not offence dates.

entries.title: The trooper page for Wednesday was published after the previous reading; the page for Thursday is not published yet
body: The Alaska State Troopers daily dispatch page for Oct. 14 now carries the header Press Release of Wednesday, October 14, 2026 and three D Detachment items. At the previous reading it carried no date after Press Release of and no detachment headings at all, and no figure was claimed for it.

The three items are a DUI, refusal and failure-to-yield arrest, posted at 8:21 a.m.; the Oct. 12 hit and run recorded above, posted at 9:31 a.m.; and the North Pole death investigation recorded above, posted at 11:02 p.m. The arrest entry records a traffic stop at Airport Way and Gillam Way at approximately 01:38 on Oct. 14 for speeding, which the entry says became a failure to yield, and that the driver, Tatiana Moonin-Theile, age 22 as the release states it, was arrested on charges the troopers record as DUI, refusal and failure to yield and remanded to the Fairbanks Correctional Center. The court file, 4FA-26-02084CR, records one count as charging document pending with no degree of offence, so no charge class is stated here. She is charged, not convicted.

The page for Oct. 15 returns the site's blank state, with no date in the header and the line No news reported for this date, so no figure is claimed for Oct. 15. The pages for Oct. 8 to Oct. 13 hold the same incident numbers they held at the previous reading, at nine, five, five, two, three and two items. The Wildlife Troopers block was read on every page: five read No news reported and two carry one item each, at Eklutna Lake and on the Talkeetna River, both far outside the coverage area. The Fairbanks Police Department's Facebook page was reached behind a login wall with a single post visible, so it is recorded as partially reached rather than read.

entries.title: Five case files state six charges and the public database serves five of them
body: Five files read this morning carry a control reading Load All 6 Party Charges and display five charges: 4FA-26-02067CR, 4FA-26-01946CR, 4FA-26-01644CR, 4NE-26-00103CR and 4NE-26-00096CR. The control was exercised on each one and returned the same five charges each time. On 4NE-26-00096CR the five served are numbered 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6, so the count the database withholds there is the fifth and not the last; on the other four there is no way to tell from the database which of the six is absent.

On 4FA-26-02067CR and 4NE-26-00103CR all six counts are printed in the weekly charges report, which prints charge lines rather than paginating them, and are recorded in full. On 4FA-26-01946CR and 4FA-26-01644CR the sixth count appears in neither weekly report and is not known; the charge figures published for those two files are five of six and the sixth is recorded as unknown rather than guessed at.

The limit is a display limit on a public terminal and not a sealed or missing charge. It also means that a charge count taken from the public database alone, on any file with more than five counts, is short.

entries.title: One item added to the state press index, from outside the area, and still nothing published on the dismissed murder charge
body: The Alaska Department of Law press index carries 157 release anchors under its 2026 path, against 156 at the previous reading by the same method. The item added is dated 10/14/26 and records a Kodiak jury convicting a corrections officer of sexual assault in the third degree, which is outside the coverage area and the second Kodiak item in three days. The newest item inside the coverage area remains the 10/05/26 release recording a Fairbanks conviction on two Class B felony counts of sexual abuse of a minor in the second degree, already carried.

Six days after the court recorded the single first-degree murder count in 4FA-26-00112CR as dismissed on a finding that the defendant was incompetent and closed the case, the department has published nothing about it, and no newsroom read here has carried it. A dismissed charge is not a conviction and the court file states no finding about the alleged conduct.

The U.S. Attorney index for the District of Alaska carries twelve rows, identical in membership to the last three transcriptions. The newest row is dated Oct. 7 and is outside the coverage area; nothing inside the coverage area on that index is newer than Sept. 18. A direct request was refused at the gateway for a second consecutive morning and the index was read by another non-browser route, which establishes the membership of the index and nothing finer.

The News-Miner public safety column of Oct. 14 was read in full and carries three Interior items: the North Pole plea recorded above, the Oct. 10 burglary and assault charges on 4FA-26-02067CR already carried, and the Nenana-filed 4NE-26-00103CR, which the column places as arising from a single-vehicle rollover near Anderson Road with an arraignment on Oct. 10 and bail of $2,500. The KTVF crime index carries 55 rows, newest Oct. 14 and outside the area; its newest Interior item remains Sept. 18. Alaska's News Source carries 56 rows, newest Oct. 14 and outside the area, and its newest Fairbanks item is Oct. 3. Your Alaska Link added three items overnight, all outside the area, and carries nothing inside the coverage area newer than Oct. 8.

PulsePoint, the Fairbanks Emergency Communications Center feed, carried 48 incidents in its rolling window: 34 medical emergencies, 4 public service calls, 4 fire alarms, 2 railroad or train emergencies, 1 fire, 1 traffic collision, 1 investigation and 1 elevator rescue. The traffic collision was logged at 7:46 a.m. on Oct. 14 and its location is recorded only as a pair of coordinates with no street; it appears in no police or trooper feed read this morning. This feed has no police or crime incident type, medical calls are posted at street level only, and nothing on it is published as a crime.
